catalog_quote: 5）アクセント アクセントに関しては不明の部分が多く確実に言えることは少ないが，以下のことが推測可能であると考えられる。a）資料が断片的かつ非常に語数に制約があり，その信憑性は必ずしも高いとは言えないが，ピッチアクセントであると考えられると共に母音の長短も弁別的である可能性もある。b）ピッチアクセントであるとするならば，北海道方言と同じように低から高への上昇が弁別的である。この上昇点より前の音節はすべて低く，その後ろの音節は次第に下降したと考えられる。c）アクセント核の位置は，方言差もあったであろうが，現時点では北海道方言と同じような傾向があったと見られる。d）母音の長短も弁別的であったとするならば，ピッチアクセントとは全く無関係に存在した可能性もある。これはアクセントの高いところが母音が長いという対応関係を文献は必ずしも示していないことによる。 [pp. 88-89, sec. 1.a 5), the Hokkaido rule referred to:] a）高低アクセントが音韻上の区別を行う。b）日本語と逆で，低から高への上昇が弁別的である。この上昇点より前の音節はすべて低く，その後ろの音節は次第に下降する。… d）アクセント核の位置は，北海道方言でも差があるが，多くの方言で次のような傾向がある。1．第一音節が開音節であるならば，アクセント核は第二音節にある。sapa LH「頭」；sapaha LHL「彼の頭」；kusapaha LHLL「私の頭」 第一音節が開音節でもアクセント核が第一音節にある語がある。tere HL「待つ」；pase HL「重い」；teta HL「ここに」 2．第一音節が閉音節であるならば，アクセント核は第一音節にある。sikup HL「育つ」；penram HL「胸」；notkir HL「あご」

new_statements.translation: 5) Accent. Much about the accent is unknown and little can be said with certainty, but the following can be inferred. a) The materials are fragmentary and very limited in the number of words, and their reliability is not necessarily high, but [the Kuril dialect] is considered to have had pitch accent, and vowel length may also have been distinctive. b) If it was pitch accent, then as in the Hokkaido dialects the rise from Low to High was distinctive; all syllables before the point of rise were low and the syllables after it gradually fell. c) The position of the accent nucleus, though there were probably dialect differences, appears at present to have had the same tendency as the Hokkaido dialects. [p. 89, on Hokkaido:] The position of the accent nucleus differs even among Hokkaido dialects, but most dialects show the following tendency: 1. if the first syllable is open, the accent nucleus is on the second syllable ... there are (some) words whose first syllable is open but whose nucleus is on the first syllable ... 2. if the first syllable is closed, the accent nucleus is on the first syllable.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Kuril Ainu (extinct; known only from 18th-early 20th c. wordlists) is inferred to have had a Hokkaido-type pitch accent: one Low-to-High rise per word whose location follows syllable weight at the left edge -- accent on the first syllable if it is closed (heavy), otherwise on the second syllable. The author flags this as inference from fragmentary records, allows for dialect differences, and leaves open that vowel length was (also, perhaps independently) distinctive.
new_statements.secondary_stress: None described for Kuril; syllables after the accentual rise are said to fall gradually (no secondary prominence).
new_statements.exceptions: Itabashi: probable dialect differences within Kuril; Hokkaido-type lexical exceptions with initial accent on an open first syllable (tere, pase, teta) are noted for the model system; vowel length in the records is inconsistently marked and may have been independent of pitch (d), p. 92). Murayama 1971 (NDL frame 147) adds a morphological case from Krasheninnikov's accent marks: possessive 'personal forms' of monosyllabic consonant-final stems (ku-ip-i, ku-ak-i, ku-mac-i) are accented on the 2nd syllable in North Kuril Ainu, 'as in Hokkaido'. Bugaeva & Satō 2021 (pp. 199-200) note a Kuril-specific loss of /h/ in accented heavy syllables (ór.kew < hórkew) and rare /h/-loss before unaccented vowels, presupposing the same weight rule.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level accent of citation forms as recoverable from transcriptions (Krasheninnikov 1738/1755 with acute/grave accent marks, Dybowski/Radliński 1892, Torii 1903, Voznesenskij <=1843; Golovnin 1811 in Bugaeva & Satō); no phrase-level information; no audio exists (last speakers gone by mid-20th c.). The statement is explicitly hedged ('推測可能', '傾向があったと見られる').
new_statements.identity_note: Itabashi's '千島方言' pools the Northern Kuril (Shumshu/Paramushir) records of Krasheninnikov (1738/1755), Voznesenskij (<=1843), Dybowski/Radliński (1892) and Torii (1903) -- i.e. North Kuril Ainu, the core of Glottolog kuri1271; Murayama 1971's remark is explicitly about 北千島アイヌ語 (North Kuril). Bugaeva & Satō 2021 separate Northern Kuril from Southern Kuril (Kunashir/Iturup, lexically closer to NE Hokkaido Ainu, ainu1240); their accent remarks apply the pan-Ainu rule to both. The model system referred to throughout is Hokkaido Ainu (ainu1240) pitch accent; Sakhalin Ainu (sakh1245) instead has distinctive vowel length.
